sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca loke 'smin dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha jñānayogena sāṃkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām
english: The Blessed Lord said: In this world a twofold path was taught of old by me, O blameless one — that of knowledge for the followers of Sāṃkhya, and that of action for those devoted to yoga.

sanskrit: na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śnute na ca saṃnyasanād eva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati
english: Not by abstaining from actions does a man attain freedom from action, nor by renunciation alone does he reach perfection.

sanskrit: na hi kaś cit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarmakṛt kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijair guṇaiḥ
english: For no one ever, even for a moment, remains without performing action; everyone is driven to act, helplessly, by the qualities born of material nature.

sanskrit: karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
english: He who, restraining the organs of action, sits dwelling in his mind upon the objects of sense — that deluded soul is called a hypocrite.

sanskrit: yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate 'rjuna karmendriyaiḥ karmayogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
english: But he who, restraining the senses with the mind, O Arjuna, undertakes through the organs of action the yoga of action, unattached — he excels.

sanskrit: niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasidhyed akarmaṇaḥ
english: Perform your appointed action, for action is better than inaction; even the maintenance of your body could not be accomplished without action.

sanskrit: yajñārthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra loko 'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara
english: Save for action performed for the sake of sacrifice, this world is bound by action; therefore, O son of Kuntī, perform action for that purpose, free from attachment.

sanskrit: sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo 'stv iṣṭakāmadhuk
english: Having of old created mankind together with sacrifice, the Lord of Creatures said: By this shall you bring forth offspring; let this be the cow that yields all your desires.

sanskrit: devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha
english: By this nourish the gods, and let the gods nourish you; nourishing one another, you shall attain the highest good.

sanskrit: iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
english: For the gods, nourished by sacrifice, will grant you the enjoyments you desire; but he who enjoys their gifts without offering anything in return to them is verily a thief.

sanskrit: yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ bhuñjate te tv aghaṃ pāpā ye pacanty ātmakāraṇāt
english: The good, who eat the remnants of sacrifice, are freed from all sins; but the wicked, who cook only for their own sake, partake of evil.

sanskrit: annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād annasaṃbhavaḥ yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ
english: From food creatures come into being; from rain food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain; and sacrifice is born of action.

sanskrit: karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam tasmāt sarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
english: Know that action springs from Brahman, and Brahman springs from the Imperishable; therefore the all-pervading Brahman is ever established in sacrifice.

sanskrit: evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati
english: He who in this world does not keep turning the wheel thus set in motion lives in vain, O Pārtha — a man of sinful life, delighting in the senses.

sanskrit: yas tv ātmaratir eva syād ātmatṛptaś ca mānavaḥ ātmany eva ca saṃtuṣṭas tasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
english: But the man whose delight is in the Self alone, who is content in the Self, and satisfied within the Self — for him there exists no duty to be done.

sanskrit: naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaś cana na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaś cid arthavyapāśrayaḥ
english: For him there is no purpose whatever in what is done, nor any in what is left undone; nor has he any need to depend upon any being among all creatures.

sanskrit: tasmād asaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ
english: Therefore, ever unattached, perform the action that ought to be done; for performing action without attachment, a man attains the Supreme.

sanskrit: karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ lokasaṃgraham evāpi saṃpaśyan kartum arhasi
english: For by action alone did Janaka and others attain perfection; and with regard to the welfare of the world too, you ought to act.

sanskrit: yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
english: Whatever a great man does, that very thing other people do; whatever standard he sets, the world follows it.

sanskrit: na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃ cana nānavāptam avāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi
english: For me, O Pārtha, there is nothing whatever to be done in the three worlds, nothing unattained that need be attained; yet I remain engaged in action.

sanskrit: yadi hy ahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
english: For if I did not remain ever tirelessly engaged in action, men would follow my path in every way, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṃ karma ced aham saṃkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
english: These worlds would fall to ruin if I did not perform action; I would be the author of confusion and would destroy these creatures.

sanskrit: saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata kuryād vidvāṃs tathāsaktaś cikīrṣur lokasaṃgraham
english: As the ignorant act, attached to action, O Bhārata, so should the wise man act, but unattached, desiring the welfare of the world.

sanskrit: na buddhibhedaṃ janayed ajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām joṣayet sarvakarmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran
english: Let him not unsettle the understanding of the ignorant who are attached to action; the wise man, himself disciplined, should engage in all actions and so encourage them to do likewise.

sanskrit: prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ ahaṃkāravimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate
english: Actions are in every way performed by the qualities of material nature; but he whose soul is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am the doer."

sanskrit: tattvavit tu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
english: But he who knows the truth, O mighty-armed, about the divisions of the qualities and of action, recognizing that it is the qualities that act upon the qualities, does not become attached.

sanskrit: prakṛter guṇasaṃmūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu tān akṛtsnavido mandān kṛtsnavin na vicālayet
english: Those deluded by the qualities of material nature become attached to the actions of those qualities; but let not the man of complete knowledge unsettle those dull ones of incomplete knowledge.

sanskrit: mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ
english: Surrendering all actions to me, with your mind fixed on the Supreme Self, and becoming free from longing and from the sense of "mine," fight, your fever gone.

sanskrit: ye me matam idaṃ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ śraddhāvanto 'nasūyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiḥ
english: Those men who constantly follow this teaching of mine, full of faith and free from cavil, they too are released from the bondage of actions.

sanskrit: ye tv etad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ
english: But those who, cavilling at it, do not follow this teaching of mine — know them to be deluded in all knowledge, mindless, and lost.

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
english: Even the man of knowledge acts in accordance with his own nature; beings follow their nature — what can restraint accomplish?

sanskrit: indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau tayor na vaśam āgacchet tau hy asya paripanthinau
english: In the object of each sense, attraction and aversion are seated; let none come under their sway, for they are his two waylayers.

sanskrit: śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ
english: Better is one's own duty, though imperfectly done, than the duty of another well performed; better is death in one's own duty — the duty of another is fraught with danger.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca atha kena prayukto 'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ anicchann api vārṣṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ
english: Arjuna said: But impelled by what does a man commit sin, O Vārṣṇeya, even against his will, as if driven by force?

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam
english: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is wrath, born of the quality of passion, all-devouring and most sinful — know this to be the enemy here.

sanskrit: dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśo malena ca yatholbenāvṛto garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛtam
english: As fire is obscured by smoke, and a mirror by dust, as an embryo is enveloped by the womb's membrane, so is this enveloped by that.

sanskrit: āvṛtaṃ jñānam etena jñānino nityavairiṇā kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca
english: Knowledge is enveloped by this constant enemy of the wise, O son of Kuntī — in the form of desire, an insatiable fire.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam ucyate etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam
english: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these it deludes the embodied one, veiling his knowledge.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau niyamya bharatarṣabha pāpmānaṃ prajahihy enaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam
english: Therefore, O bull among the Bharatas, first restraining the senses, cast off this sinful thing, the destroyer of knowledge and discrimination.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ
english: The senses, they say, are great; greater than the senses is the mind; greater than the mind is the intellect; but greater than the intellect is He.

sanskrit: evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānam ātmanā jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam
english: Thus knowing Him who is beyond the intellect, and steadying the self by the Self, slay, O mighty-armed, the enemy in the form of desire, hard to overcome.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavān aham avyayam vivasvān manave prāha manur ikṣvākave 'bravīt
english: The Blessed Lord said: This imperishable yoga I declared to Vivasvat; Vivasvat told it to Manu; and Manu spoke it to Ikṣvāku.

sanskrit: evaṃ paraṃparāprāptam imaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ paraṃtapa
english: Thus received in succession, the royal sages knew it; but through the long lapse of time that yoga was lost here, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: sa evāyaṃ mayā te 'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ bhakto 'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hy etad uttamam
english: That very same ancient yoga has today been declared by me to you, for you are my devotee and my friend; and this is the supreme secret.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ katham etad vijānīyāṃ tvam ādau proktavān iti
english: Arjuna said: Later was your birth, earlier the birth of Vivasvat; how then am I to understand this — that you declared it in the beginning?

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna tāny ahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha paraṃtapa
english: The Blessed Lord said: Many are the births that have passed for me and for you, O Arjuna; all of them I know, but you do not know them, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: ajo 'pi sann avyayātmā bhūtānām īśvaro 'pi san prakṛtiṃ svām adhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmy ātmamāyayā
english: Though I am unborn and of imperishable Self, though I am the Lord of all beings, yet, governing my own material nature, I come into being through my own power of illusion.

sanskrit: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham
english: For whenever there is a decline of righteousness, O Bhārata, and a rising up of unrighteousness, then I send forth myself.

sanskrit: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge
english: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the firm establishment of righteousness, I come into being age after age.

sanskrit: janma karma ca me divyam evaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna
english: He who thus knows in truth my divine birth and action, on leaving the body is not born again, but comes to me, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā mām upāśritāḥ bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvam āgatāḥ
english: Freed from passion, fear, and wrath, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, have come to my state of being.

sanskrit: ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tathaiva bhajāmy aham mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
english: In whatever way men approach me, in that same way do I favor them; in every way, O Pārtha, men follow my path.

sanskrit: kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā
english: Desiring the fruition of their actions, men here worship the gods; for swiftly in the world of men comes the success born of action.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ tasya kartāram api māṃ viddhy akartāram avyayam
english: The fourfold order was created by me according to the divisions of quality and action; though I am its author, know me to be the non-doer, the changeless.

sanskrit: na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā iti māṃ yo 'bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate
english: Actions do not taint me, nor have I any longing for the fruit of action; he who knows me thus is not bound by actions.

sanskrit: evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvair api mumukṣubhiḥ kuru karmaiva tasmāt tvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam
english: Knowing this, the ancient seekers of liberation also performed action; therefore do you too perform action, as it was done by those of old in former times.

sanskrit: kiṃ karma kim akarmeti kavayo 'py atra mohitāḥ tat te karma pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt
english: What is action, what is inaction? — even the wise are bewildered here. I shall declare to you that action, knowing which you shall be freed from evil.

sanskrit: karmaṇo hy api boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ akarmaṇaś ca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ
english: For the nature of action must be understood, and the nature of wrong action must be understood, and the nature of inaction too must be understood; profound is the course of action.

sanskrit: karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed akarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt
english: He who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is wise among men; he is disciplined, a doer of all action.

sanskrit: yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṃkalpavarjitāḥ jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ
english: He whose every undertaking is free from the prompting of desire, whose actions are burned up in the fire of knowledge — him the wise call a sage.

sanskrit: tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ karmaṇy abhipravṛtto 'pi naiva kiṃ cit karoti saḥ
english: Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, ever content, depending on nothing, even when fully engaged in action he does nothing at all.

sanskrit: nirāśīr yatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam
english: Free from longing, his mind and self restrained, having relinquished all possessions, performing action with the body alone, he incurs no sin.

sanskrit: yadṛcchālābhasaṃtuṣṭo dvaṃdvātīto vimatsaraḥ samaḥ siddhāv asiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate
english: Content with what comes unsought, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, even-minded in success and in failure — though he acts, he is not bound.

sanskrit: gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate
english: For one who is free from attachment, liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, who acts for the sake of sacrifice — his whole action dissolves away.

sanskrit: brahmārpaṇaṃ brahmahavir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā
english: Brahman is the offering, Brahman the oblation, poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman; Brahman alone is to be reached by him who meditates upon Brahman in his action.

sanskrit: daivam evāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate brahmāgnāv apare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati
english: Some yogins perform sacrifice to the gods alone, while others offer the sacrifice itself as oblation into the fire of Brahman.

sanskrit: śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati śabdādīn viṣayān anya indriyāgniṣu juhvati
english: Some offer the senses, hearing and the rest, into the fires of restraint; others offer sound and the other objects of sense into the fires of the senses.

sanskrit: sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite
english: And others offer all the activities of the senses and the activities of the vital breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

sanskrit: dravyayajñās tapoyajñā yogayajñās tathāpare svādhyāyajñānayajñāś ca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: Some make sacrifice with material things, some with austerity, some with yoga; and others, ascetics of strict vows, sacrifice with study of scripture and with knowledge.

sanskrit: apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe 'pānaṃ tathāpare prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Some offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and likewise the incoming into the outgoing, restraining the courses of inhalation and exhalation, intent upon the control of breath.

sanskrit: apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati sarve 'py ete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ
english: Others, with regulated diet, offer the vital breaths into the vital breaths; all these indeed are knowers of sacrifice, their impurities consumed by sacrifice.

sanskrit: yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam nāyaṃ loko 'sty ayajñasya kuto 'nyaḥ kurusattama
english: Those who feed on the nectar of the remnants of sacrifice go to the eternal Brahman; this world is not for him who offers no sacrifice — how then the other, O best of the Kurus?

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe karmajān viddhi tān sarvān evaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase
english: Thus manifold sacrifices are spread out before the face of Brahman; know them all to be born of action, and knowing this, you shall be liberated.

sanskrit: śreyān dravyamayād yajñāj jñānayajñaḥ paraṃtapa sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
english: Better than the sacrifice of material things is the sacrifice of knowledge, O scorcher of foes; all action in its entirety, O Pārtha, culminates in knowledge.

sanskrit: tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninas tattvadarśinaḥ
english: Know that by humble reverence, by inquiry, and by service; the wise, the seers of truth, will instruct you in that knowledge.

sanskrit: yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava yena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi
english: Knowing which you shall not again fall into such delusion, O son of Pāṇḍu, and through which you shall see all beings, without exception, within yourself and then in me.

sanskrit: api ced asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ saṃtariṣyasi
english: Even if you were the most sinful of all sinners, by the raft of knowledge alone you shall cross over all wickedness.

sanskrit: yathaidhāṃsi samiddho 'gnir bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā
english: As a kindled fire reduces firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ashes.

sanskrit: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitram iha vidyate tat svayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati
english: For there exists here no purifier equal to knowledge; he who is himself perfected in yoga finds it in time within his own self.

sanskrit: śraddhāvāṃl labhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntim acireṇādhigacchati
english: The man of faith, devoted to it and master of his senses, attains knowledge; and having attained knowledge, he quickly reaches the supreme peace.
